questions.q: What six traits make up the SUCCES model for sticky ideas?
a: Simple, unexpected, concrete, credible, emotional and stories
Short, urgent, clever, current, entertaining and shareable
Specific, useful, clear, consistent, engaging and surprising
Simple, unique, colorful, convincing, exciting and structured
questions.why: The overview spells out the acronym: simple, unexpected, concrete, credible, emotional and stories.

questions.q: Why do sticky ideas need to be unexpected?
a: People ignore what fails to surprise them, so it never gets noticed
Surprise makes an idea easier to remember word for word
Unexpected claims are automatically more credible to audiences
People only trust ideas that contradict what they already know
questions.why: Lesson 1 says if something does not stand out it is as if it is not there, so surprise earns attention.

a: Showing people they lack an important piece of knowledge and letting them seek it
Leaving key details vague so your audience has to guess your meaning
Asking a question you already know the answer to
Promising a reward before revealing any useful information
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines it as convincing people something important is missing and giving them a way to find out.

questions.q: Which three story patterns does the summary describe?
a: Challenge, reaching out and creativity
Conflict, recovery and discovery
Rags to riches, revenge and romance
Warning, instruction and inspiration
questions.why: Lesson 3 names challenge, reaching out and creativity as timeless patterns for stories that stick.

questions.q: What does the Subway example illustrate about making ideas stick?
a: A memorable customer story can be more powerful than advertising claims
Discounts and promotions are the most reliable way to attract buyers
Health claims only work when backed by official statistics
Long-running campaigns matter more than any single story
questions.why: Lesson 3 contrasts ordinary slogans with the story of a man who lost 200 pounds eating Subway.
